newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler to build new Toledo Jeep plant - paper.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler to build new Toledo Jeep plant - paper.

text.p: Chrysler Corp has reached a tentative agreement with local and state officials in Toledo, Ohio, to invest $1.2 billion and build a new assembly plant in the city, the Toledo Blade reported Monday.

According to the paper, the U.S. No. 3 automaker would build a new 1.1 million square-foot plant at its Stickney Avenue site, almost doubling the existing facility. The money would also be used to upgrade Chrysler's Jeep Parkway plant.
Plans call for Chrysler to move production of its higher-volume Jeep Cherokee Sport to the new Stickney facility from the Parkway site. Wrangler production would be shifted to Parkway from Stickney.
"The 'i's' have been dotted and the 't's' have been crossed," the paper quoted Toledo Mayor Carty Finkbeiner as saying.
The deal still has to be approved by Chrysler executives, including Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Robert Eaton, the paper said, adding an announcement could be made as early as Monday.

The two plants currently employ about 6,000 people and produce 1,200 vehicles a day, according to the paper. It said the new and upgraded plants would have fewer workers but would try to keep 4,900 employees.
